costPage.intro: Bluetail Medical Group does not publish a price list, so any figure attached to it comes from patients rather than from the clinic. The rows below are gathered from public sources and should be read as rough market context for a US orthopaedic injection practice, not as a quote and not as anything the clinic has confirmed. What you actually pay is set at consultation and written up in a Good Faith Estimate, which the clinic will issue on request. Read it as context for your quote, not as your quote.
costPage.introEmpty: Bluetail Medical Group publishes no prices. Not on the services pages, not on the platelet rich plasma or bone marrow aspirate concentrate pages, and not on the FAQ, which discusses insurance and financing without naming a single figure. The quote is built at consultation and turns on which procedure the physician recommends, platelet rich plasma being the cheaper option and a bone marrow concentrate injection the dearer one, on how many sites are being injected, and on how many treatments are planned, since the clinic says the average patient has one or two and occasionally three, spaced 12 to 16 weeks apart. Before that consultation the clinic requires an X ray or MRI, which you obtain and pay for elsewhere unless you are seen at the St. Louis office, and it usually orders blood work. Ask for a written Good Faith Estimate covering the whole course rather than a single visit, and ask separately what the imaging, labs and any brace add.
includes: Nothing is itemised publicly, so the only document that will tell you what your money buys is the Good Faith Estimate. By law it has to cover the procedure plus related costs such as medical tests, prescription drugs and supplies, so ask for it in writing before you commit.
Ultrasound or fluoroscopic guidance during the injection, which the clinic describes as its standard technique. It does not say whether that is billed separately.
The procedure visit itself, which the clinic says runs 1 to 2 hours.
excludes: Imaging. The clinic requires an X ray or MRI before your first visit and says you must obtain it elsewhere and send it in, unless you are being seen at the St. Louis office, which can take an X ray on site.
Blood work. The clinic says it will most likely order labs at the initial evaluation, covering complete blood count, testosterone and vitamin D.

Supplements. If your testosterone or vitamin D reads low the physician is likely to suggest supplementing it. The clinic calls this optional and not required for treatment, so treat it as a line you can decline.
A knee brace, which the clinic says may be prescribed during the evaluation for knee patients.
Repeat treatments. The clinic says the average patient has one or two and rarely three, spaced 12 to 16 weeks apart, so a per treatment figure is not the course total.
Travel. The group runs sites in Missouri, Florida, California and Indiana, and nothing on the site suggests travel or accommodation is priced in.
costPage.insuranceNote: Assume you are paying yourself. The clinic states plainly that most insurance companies do not cover these procedures and consider them investigational, which is the standard US position on platelet rich plasma and bone marrow concentrate injections. Nothing on the site mentions HSA or FSA eligibility either way, so check that with your plan administrator rather than the front desk. Because this is self pay care, the federal No Surprises rules apply and the clinic publishes its Good Faith Estimate policy: you can ask for a written estimate before scheduling, you are meant to receive it at least one business day ahead, and a final bill that comes in at least 400 USD above the estimate can be disputed. That 400 USD is a legal threshold, not a fee.
costPage.financingNote: The clinic offers patient financing through CareCredit and names no other partner. There is no published deposit policy, no payment plan detail, no cancellation terms and no statement on whether the consultation is charged separately from the procedure, so all of that has to come out of the phone call. The number for estimates is 636-778-2900. Worth asking for the whole course to be costed on one document, since the clinic's own FAQ points at one to three treatments rather than one, and worth asking what happens to your money if the physician decides at the evaluation that you are not a candidate.

faqs.question: How much does Bluetail Medical Group cost?
faqs.answer: Bluetail Medical Group does not publish prices, so there is no list price to quote. The only figures in circulation come from patients writing public reviews, who have described paying around 3,200 USD for a course of stem cell and platelet rich plasma injections and around 11,000 USD for a back procedure combining bone marrow cells with platelet rich plasma. Those are one person's bill each, unverified and possibly years old, so treat them as a rough sense of scale rather than a price. Your own number comes from the consultation, and you can ask for it in writing as a Good Faith Estimate before you schedule anything.

faqs.question: What actually drives the quote?
faqs.answer: Four things, on the clinic's own account. Which procedure is recommended, since platelet rich plasma is drawn from blood and a bone marrow aspirate concentrate injection is a bigger procedure that costs more. How many sites are being injected. How many treatments are planned, and the clinic says the average patient has one or two, rarely three, spaced 12 to 16 weeks apart. And what the workup adds, meaning the X ray or MRI you have to bring, the blood work the clinic orders, and any brace or supplement suggested afterwards.

faqs.question: Will insurance cover it?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not, and the clinic says so itself: most insurers do not cover these procedures and treat them as investigational. It offers CareCredit financing instead, which tells you the same thing. If you want to try an HSA or FSA card, confirm eligibility with your plan administrator first, because the clinic's site takes no position on it.

faqs.question: What should I ask before booking?
faqs.answer: Ask for a written Good Faith Estimate that covers the full recommended course rather than one visit, since the clinic itself expects one to three treatments. Ask whether the consultation is billed separately from the procedure, and what it costs if you decide not to proceed. Ask what the imaging and lab work cost, and whether you can get them done cheaper through your own physician. And ask what the estimate assumes about the number of joints or sites, because that is the easiest line for a quote to grow on.

costPage.intro: Cellinique does not put a price on any of its cell based programs. Its own pricing page says quotes are given only after a consultation with Dr. Kim Gun Woo, and the clinic points to Korea's medical advertising rules as the reason it will not post figures publicly. The numbers below are the only Cellinique prices we could find stated anywhere, and they come from the clinic's listings on the Korean booking platform Cashdoc, which notes the prices were set by the clinic itself. Read them as a sense of where this clinic sits, not as your quote.
costPage.introEmpty: Cellinique does not publish prices. Its pricing page carries no figures at all, and both the NovaStem and SVF treatment pages send you to the non reimbursed fee disclosure or to a consultation instead of naming an amount. The clinic states that under Korea's Medical Service Act it will not advertise non reimbursed fees or discounts, so the amount is set case by case after Dr. Kim Gun Woo reviews your skin condition, medical history and treatment goals. What moves the number is the treatment category, whether fat harvesting is involved, how much area and volume are treated, how many sessions are planned, and whether other procedures are bundled in. Ask for the quote in writing, split into harvest, processing, application and aftercare, and ask which of those four stages the total already covers.

Because these are non reimbursed items, each Korean clinic sets its own fee, and the clinic's own cost guide suggests checking the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service published non covered fee data as a baseline before you compare quotes.

Refunds before treatment follow the policy explained at consultation, and the clinic says refunds may be limited once part of a treatment has been carried out. Cellinique also runs periodic promotions on its events page, which in mid 2026 carried discounted prices on lasers, boosters and filler, so it is worth asking what is running when you book.

faqs.question: How much does Cellinique Clinic cost?
faqs.answer: There is no published price for the cell based programs, so the honest answer is that you will not know until you have had a consultation. The only Cellinique figures stated publicly are on the Korean platform Cashdoc, where the clinic lists fat grafting at 1,650,000 KRW against a 1,900,000 KRW list price, a full face Titanium laser session at 1,100,000 KRW, and Rejuran Healer 2cc at 550,000 KRW, all with VAT included. NovaStem, SVF, Face Cell, DermaCell, NK Cell and PRF carry no public number at all.

faqs.question: Why will the clinic not publish a price for NovaStem or SVF?
faqs.answer: Cellinique gives two reasons. The first is legal: it says Korea's Medical Service Act restricts advertising discounts or waivers on non reimbursed fees, so it does not post amounts or discount rates on public pages. The second is that the quote depends on the treatment area and scope, the volume used, the number of sessions and whether other procedures are combined. It says the detailed non reimbursed fee disclosure can be reviewed in the clinic or requested on 02 6203 3434.

faqs.question: What should I ask for so the quote can be compared?
faqs.answer: The clinic's own cost guide gives a useful checklist, so hold it to that. Ask for the total split into four lines, fat harvest, separation and processing, application, and aftercare, and ask which of those the figure already covers. Then pin down whether the price is per session or for a course, which areas and what volume are being treated, whether the anaesthesia fee is inside the total, how many follow up visits are included, and what happens to the fee if the plan changes after the health assessment. Get it in writing rather than as a verbal total.

faqs.question: Is a stem cell quote in Seoul comparable across clinics?
faqs.answer: Not directly, and Cellinique says so itself. Clinics bundle the same named procedure differently, and quotes that both say stem cells may be pricing very different things, for example a same day fat derived cell fraction against a pathway that involves culturing cells. Match the process description to the price before you compare totals, and treat any single advertised number as a starting point rather than the cost of your plan.

faqs.question: How much does Chaum cost?

Your bill will differ, because materials, drugs, sedation and contrast are added on top and several rows change with dose and area treated.

faqs.question: Does Chaum publish a price for stem cell therapy?
faqs.answer: Only for cosmetic fat grafting with stem cells and for its Evercell skin line. There is no published figure for an intravenous or joint stem cell injection at Chaum, and its immune, power aging and detox clinic pages carry no prices at all. If you are asking about anything other than the cosmetic rows, you are in private quote territory.

faqs.question: Why do men and women pay different prices for the same check-up?

faqs.question: Is the published range what I will actually be charged?

Treat the list as a floor and ask for a written itemised quote before you commit.

faqs.question: How much does Gangnam JS Hospital cost?
faqs.answer: Its English site publishes guide bands of roughly 450,000 to 950,000 won for a single site image guided injection and 250,000 to 650,000 won for an IV session, but the cord blood cell knee cartilage surgery it is best known for has no published price and is quoted only after a consultation and imaging. So a wellness or injection visit can be budgeted from the site, and the knee operation cannot.

faqs.question: Why is there no price for the knee cartilage surgery?
faqs.answer: The hospital simply does not publish one. Its Korean pages, its English pages and its dedicated knee page all describe the procedure at length and none of them names a figure. Korean price aggregators list other hospitals for the same product but not this one, so there is no published number to compare against either. Expect a private quote and ask what it covers.

faqs.question: What should I ask when I request a quote?

Confirm whether it covers one knee or both, whether a bow leg correction is being done in the same operation, how many nights of inpatient stay are assumed and what an extra night costs, whether imaging and follow up visits are inside the number or billed separately, and what happens to the price if the plan changes after the imaging review. For injections and IVs, ask which add-ons the quoted session already includes.

faqs.question: Are the published ranges the price I will pay?
faqs.answer: No. The hospital labels them as a guide and states that the final quote follows an imaging review and the plan you select. The bands are wide, roughly double from bottom to top on several services, and add-ons and labs sit outside them. Use them to work out whether this hospital is in your budget bracket, then get a written quote.

Travel, accommodation and interpreting, none of which the clinic prices.
costPage.insuranceNote: This matters more for Korean residents than for overseas patients. The clinic states that stem cell treatment for knee arthritis has been designated a new medical technology and is covered, and separately that Korean actual loss insurers are pushing back on the 6 hour admission rule that payment for the fat derived injection depends on. By the clinic's own account that argument is live, so treat cover as something to get in writing from your insurer rather than something the clinic can settle for you. Nothing on the site mentions US insurance, HSA or FSA, and overseas patients should assume self pay.
costPage.financingNote: The clinic publishes no payment plan, no deposit policy and no financing partner. Prices appear in Korean won only, with no international payment terms and no note on cards, cash or wire, so ask which currency you will actually be billed in, what deposit holds a date, and what happens if you cancel after flying. The free online consultation the site offers is the route to a written quote, and getting the whole course costed on one document is worth the extra email.

faqs.question: How much does SH Clinic cost?
faqs.answer: SH Clinic publishes its stem cell prices, and they run from 1,000,000 KRW for the entry level V-Shot tier to 10,000,000 KRW for the top P-Shot and B-Shot tiers. Knee work is listed at 5,500,000 KRW for one knee and 8,800,000 KRW for both. Most other programs sit between 2,000,000 and 6,000,000 KRW depending on which cell source the tier uses. These are the clinic's own published figures, not a quote, and the site does not price consultation or imaging.

faqs.question: Is the published price for one treatment or the whole course?
faqs.answer: The clinic does not say, and this is the single biggest gap in the list. Each program shows a price and, separately, a recommended frequency: 3 treatments at 1 to 2 month intervals for most, and 8 treatments at 2 week intervals for hair loss. Whether 2,000,000 KRW buys one of those or all eight changes the real cost by a factor of eight, so pin it down in writing before you book anything.

faqs.question: Why do the tiers cost different amounts?
faqs.answer: The clinic ties the tier to the cell source. Hematopoietic cell tiers are the cheapest and tiers using bone marrow or adipose cells cost more. Its own page attributes price variation to the type and technology of cells used, the number of administrations, and whether the cells are the patient's own or donated. The exception is the B-Shot, where four tiers are priced and no cell source is named for any of them.

faqs.question: What is not covered by the published figure?
faqs.answer: Consultation, imaging, any hospital admission and travel. The knee programs are gated on an MRI or X-ray grade and the clinic publishes no fee for that assessment, nor for the admission its own page says Korean insurers expect for the fat derived injection. Ask for those as line items rather than assuming they are folded in.

faqs.question: How much does Yonsei BH Clinic cost?

faqs.question: Does the clinic publish its own prices?

faqs.question: Why is the same $22,000 shown for so many different treatments?

faqs.question: Is RE:YOUTH the same thing as Yonsei BH Clinic?

Everything is in Korean won and every figure is a single line item, not a package. Several of the regenerative lines carry the note that materials are billed separately, which is where a quote grows once you get it in writing. What you pay depends on which joint is treated, whether one side or both, which cell preparation or product is used, how much imaging has to be repeated in Seoul and whether you stay overnight. Ask for a written estimate broken out line by line, because Korean hospitals bill non-covered items separately rather than as one package figure.

faqs.question: How much does Yonsei Sarang Hospital cost?
faqs.answer: The regenerative lines on its published fee schedule run from 150,000 KRW for a single knee PRP injection to 9,000,000 KRW for the Cartistem cell product used in cartilage surgery. In between sit a bone marrow concentrate knee injection at 1,000,000 KRW plus a 2,000,000 KRW kit, and an adipose derived stromal vascular fraction knee injection at 1,700,000 KRW. Those are individual line items rather than packages, so a real invoice adds consultation, imaging, materials and any inpatient nights on top.

faqs.question: Why do so many of the prices say materials are billed separately?
faqs.answer: Because that is how the Korean non-covered schedule is structured. The procedure fee and the disposable kit or implant are filed as different lines, and the hospital prints the caveat next to the procedure. The bone marrow injection is the clearest example: 1,000,000 KRW for the procedure and 2,000,000 KRW for the kit. Always ask which materials your case needs before you treat a procedure fee as the price.

faqs.question: Is the published schedule the price a foreign patient actually pays?
faqs.answer: It is the price the hospital has filed for each item, in Korean won, and Korean hospitals are legally required to publish it. That makes it far more reliable than a brochure number, but it is still a base rather than a total. Read it as context for your quote, not as your quote.

faqs.question: What should I ask for before booking?
faqs.answer: A written estimate broken out by line, naming the procedure, the kit or product, one joint or both, the imaging you will need repeated in Seoul, the number of nights and any rehab sessions. Also ask when the line was last repriced, because several of these changed in 2025 and 2026, and ask whether an interpreter is included or charged.
